answer_text:
Here's a comprehensive guide to the **best sources for free 3D game assets** in 2026! 🎮

---

## 🏆 Top Free 3D Game Asset Sources

### 1. 🌟 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over **40,000 assets** — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colorful, and remarkably consistent across packs, and the site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio. There are also free tools like **Asset Forge** for creating your own 3D models.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 (Public Domain) — no attribution required
- 🎯 **Best for:** Prototyping, stylized & low-poly games

---

### 2. 🎨 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
Quaternius provides a large collection of low-poly 3D models completely free under the CC0 license, usable for any project — personal or commercial — without needing to give credit. The consistent, clean art style makes these assets perfect for prototyping or stylized games.
This creator has released thousands of models — characters, animals, vehicles, environments, weapons — with a signature style of clean geometry, bright colors, and charming animations. Assets come **rigged and animated**, ready to drop into Unity, Unreal, or Godot.
- ✅ **License:** CC0
- 🎯 **Best for:** Low-poly 3D games, animated characters

---

### 3. 🏔️ [PolyHaven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of **3D models, HDRIs, and textures** — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces, but they're high quality and instantly usable. No sign-up required — just download what you need.
- ✅ **License:** CC0
- 🎯 **Best for:** Realistic environments, lighting, textures

---

### 4. 🖼️ [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository with a large collection of downloadable assets. While many are for sale, there's a substantial number of free models. The platform's built-in **3D viewer** lets you inspect every angle of a model before downloading. Be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.
- ✅ **License:** Varies (CC0 / CC BY — check per model)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Community models, browsing with preview

---

### 5. 🎮 [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com)
The Unity Asset Store offers **10,000+ Unity-optimized assets** in its free section. 3D is Unity's bread and butter with 41k assets available, including plenty of low-poly meshes as well as pre-made animations — some with mocap data, others with keyframe animation.
- ✅ **License:** Varies per asset
- 🎯 **Best for:** Unity developers

---

### 6. 🕹️ [Itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie developers that also has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.
- ✅ **License:** Varies per creator
- 🎯 **Best for:** Unique & creative packs, indie style

---

### 7. 🔷 [Mixamo](https://www.mixamo.com) *(Animations)*
Mixamo offers **2,000+ free animations** with auto-rigging. It's perfect for bringing characters to life with walk, run, jump, attack, and death animations — no rigging expertise needed.
- ✅ **License:** Free for personal & commercial use (Adobe account needed)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Character animations & auto-rigging

---

### 8. 🌿 [Quixel Megascans](https://quixel.com)
Quixel released a final, offline version of Quixel Mixer along with the option to download **over 800 free Megascans assets**. Quixel is a pioneer in photogrammetry-based 3D assets, delivering photorealistic models compatible with any engine, as well as Blender, Maya, and Houdini. All assets are scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware.
- ✅ **License:** Free (check terms)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Photorealistic / AAA-quality assets

---

### 9. 🎭 [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of 2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects — all under open licenses like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 / CC-BY / GPL
- 🎯 **Best for:** Open-source projects, variety

---

### 10. 🧱 [Free3D](https://free3d.com)
A large number of models have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away, covering categories like houses, buildings, medieval, fantasy, cities, and more.
- ✅ **License:** Varies per model
- 🎯 **Best for:** Variety of categories (vehicles, weapons, characters, architecture)

---

## 📋 License Quick Reference

| License | Commercial Use | Attribution Needed |
|---|---|---|
| **CC0** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| **CC BY** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **CC BY-SA** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes + share alike |
| **Royalty-Free** | ⚠️ Usually | ⚠️ Check terms |

---

## 💡 Pro Tips
- Choose assets from the **same creator or pack** (e.g., all Quaternius or all Kenney) and don't mix photorealistic and low-poly cartoon styles — consistency is key!
- **GLB/glTF** are the recommended formats — all textures, materials, and animations are bundled in one file, with 3–5x faster loading compared to FBX, and native support in Three.js, Babylon.js, Unity, and Unreal Engine.
